correctness.rationale: The full coefficient multiplication gives an exact row-column outer-product equation. The margin map onto the equal-total-sum hyperplane is split and has kernel dimension (a-1)(b-1). If a commuting tuple has a pair with both margins nonzero, outer-product equality makes all margin pairs scalar multiples, proving the exact three-locus union. The rank-one locus is irreducible; independent vectors in the zero-total hyperplanes witness the sharp side-size-three component thresholds. Disjoint projective line counting gives the formula for all tuple lengths including the empty tuple. A direct independent multiplication-table checker passes 11 finite-field configurations; finite checks are not used to infer the general theorem.

value.rationale: The previously known pair census does not provide all pairwise commuting higher tuples or reduced irreducible-component structure. The result gives a complete arithmetic invariant across all tuple lengths and all finite field extensions for an unbounded natural class of semigroup algebras and classifies up to three geometrically irreducible branches with a sharp side-size-three transition. This is mathematically motivated by the disparity between semigroup-level nowhere commutativity and the unexpectedly large commuting loci after linearization; it is neither a random parameter slice nor merely repeating the pair count.
